classes.label: Education
classes.note: Process by which one develops abilities, attitudes and other forms of behaviour considered to have value in the society in which one lives. Use more specific descriptor.

classes.label: Educational interaction process
classes.note: Observation of student behaviour in response to various teaching attitudes.

classes.label: Educational anthropology
classes.note: Application of anthropological concepts and methods to the study of educational institutions and processes.

classes.label: Child psychology
classes.note: From birth to adolescence.

classes.label: Comparative education
classes.note: Comparative study of current educational theory and practice in different countries.

classes.label: Educational models
classes.note: Representation of an educational concept or system in a two or three-dimensional diagram or a mathematical or other analogous form.

classes.label: Educational development
classes.note: Developmental change of one or more characteristics of the educational system variables in a positive direction in terms of some valued criterion. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Curriculum development
classes.note: Systematic process of producing new curricula or improving existing ones. Involves setting out aims, content, methods, evaluation procedures.

classes.label: Educational innovations
classes.note: Changes in objectives, content or methods initiated, as a rule, in experimental situations.

classes.label: Educational reform
classes.note: Change planned or in process of implementation to a major part of a national system of education.

classes.label: Educational trends
classes.note: Changes in educational movement, either past or future, which occur in response to social, economic or environmental trends.

classes.label: Educational policy
classes.note: Official statements of goals to which the system of education is directed.

classes.label: Illiteracy
classes.note: Relates to the problem. Provision for resolving it should be handled by the "literacy" descriptors.

classes.label: Alternative education
classes.note: General term for schemes which offer an alternative to traditional institutional education or for movements which reject the notion of formal schooling.

classes.label: Computer uses in education
classes.note: The use of computers for instruction, testing, student/pupil personnel services, school administrative support services, etc. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Education and culture
classes.note: Taking into consideration of cultural factors in the educational process.

classes.label: School integration
classes.note: Refers to ethnic groups, covers also negative aspect of segregation.

classes.label: Educational indicators
classes.note: Numerical data used as benchmarks in the formulation and monitoring of educational policy.

classes.label: Educational objectives
classes.note: Intended or expected results of the educational process.

classes.label: Educational strategies
classes.note: Conversion of policy goals into operational terms, including some indication of alternative paths to reach these goals.

classes.label: Global citizenship education
classes.note: Global citizenship education aims to empower learners of all ages to assume active roles, both locally and globally, in building more peaceful, tolerant, inclusive and secure societies.

classes.label: Multilingual education
classes.note: The use of two or more languages in education, which may include the mother tongue.

classes.label: Bilingual education
classes.note: Encouragement of bilingualism through the teaching of regular courses in both the national language and a second language.

classes.label: Leisure and education
classes.note: Organized activities intended to help individuals or groups use non-work time in a manner conducive to physical and mental well-being.

classes.label: Democratization of education
classes.note: Policy of ensuring equality of educational opportunity in order to achieve universal education.

classes.label: Educational opportunities
classes.note: Availability of educational provision.

classes.label: Access to education
classes.note: Conditions, circumstances or requirements governing admittance to educational institutions or programmes.

classes.label: Educational priority areas
classes.note: Regions, localities, etc., in need of special educational action.

classes.label: School closure
classes.note: Refers to both permanent or temporary school closures. The latter can be due to crisis situations such as natural disaster, armed conflict or epidemics.

classes.label: Universal education
classes.note: System of education extending opportunities to all.

classes.label: Free education
classes.note: Non fee-paying education.

classes.label: Economics of education
classes.note: Techniques of economics applied to educational systems.

classes.label: Education and development
classes.note: Refers to the integration of education into the development process.

classes.label: Educational demand
classes.note: Consumer demand for education.

classes.label: Educational efficiency
classes.note: Degree to which educational systems are successful in optimizing the educational input/output relationship.

classes.label: Teacher supply
classes.note: Planning of manpower provision.

classes.label: Educational needs
classes.note: At the level of educational systems.

classes.label: Educational programmes
classes.note: Series of planned activities, with administrative connotation, relating to development of institutions. Do not confuse with "instructional programmes".

classes.label: Adult education programmes
classes.note: Programmes designed to provide learning opportunities for both adults who have not had adequate formal education, as well as others interested in lifelong learning.

classes.label: Exchange programmes
classes.note: Provide systematically for the exchange of students or teachers between institutions.

classes.label: Instructional programmes
classes.note: Outline of procedures, courses and subjects to be provided by an educational institution over a given period of time.

classes.label: School mapping
classes.note: Planning further provisions of educational establishments in terms of demographic and geographical factors.

classes.label: Educational forecasting
classes.note: Long term projection of educational development. May include design of scenarios for educational systems.

classes.label: Enrolment
classes.note: The total number of individuals registered as participants in a programme or activity.

classes.label: Educational wastage
classes.note: Effects of the associated problems of repetition and dropping out.

classes.label: Enrolment ratio
classes.note: Enrolment as percentage of relevant age group.

classes.label: Educational administration
classes.note: Relating to part or the whole of the educational system.

classes.label: Educational articulation
classes.note: Between levels of education or types of school.

classes.label: Educational autonomy
classes.note: Arrangements giving educational establishments at any level a degree of autonomy in administrative and programme matters.

classes.label: Academic freedom
classes.note: Liberty of educational institutions to decide courses and research, and of teachers to teach subjects, without outside coercion.

classes.label: Scientific freedom
classes.note: The right to engage in scientific enquiry, to pursue and communicate knowledge, and to associate freely in such activities.

classes.label: Educational cooperation
classes.note: At the international level.

classes.label: Educational assistance
classes.note: Provided by specialist missions to countries under international programmes.

classes.label: Educational coordination
classes.note: Coordination of different agencies and organizations concerned with education.

classes.label: Educational associations
classes.note: Voluntary bodies concerned with the administration of education.

classes.label: Educational foundations
classes.note: Provide grants or funds to finance research, services, facilities, equipment.

classes.label: Regional educational bodies
classes.note: Intergovernmental bodies grouping a number of countries.

classes.label: Accreditation (education)
classes.note: Recognition and approval of the academic standards of an educational institution by some external, impartial body of high public esteem.

classes.label: Educational governing boards
classes.note: Entrusted with some degree of control over managing the affairs of private and public institutions.

classes.label: Examination boards
classes.note: Organize the setting and marking of examinations and the recording of results.

classes.label: Educational leave
classes.note: Use in connection with paid or unpaid leave granted to employees for educational purposes.

classes.label: Fellowships
classes.note: Award to continue studies to an advanced level.

classes.label: Scholarships
classes.note: Reserve for school and undergraduate levels of education.

classes.label: Educational guidance
classes.note: Advising pupils or students on their educational progress, on career opportunities, or personal difficulties or anxieties.

classes.label: Vocational guidance
classes.note: Help given to the individual inside or outside the school system in choosing a career or occupation.

classes.label: Educational management
classes.note: Use to mean the management of educational establishments.

classes.label: Admission requirements
classes.note: Conditions (examination certificates, proof of skills, etc.) of entrance to courses of study, further study, training, etc.

classes.label: Educational levels
classes.note: Broad steps of formal educational progressions. Used as a classification in educational organization and statistics.

classes.label: Early childhood education
classes.note: From birth to the age of 8. It refers to all aspects of a child's development.

classes.label: Day nurseries
classes.note: Centres where young children may be left to be cared for, while the parents are at work or study. May include health and family services.

classes.label: Child rearing
classes.note: Refers to a set of culturally and socially determined practices, customs and beliefs.

classes.label: Higher education
classes.note: Stage following secondary education, regardless of course duration or certificate awarded.

classes.label: Primary education
classes.note: From age five to eleven.

classes.label: Educational systems
classes.note: Arrangement into an organic whole of the interdependent institutions and programmes providing formal and nonformal education.

classes.label: Adult education
classes.note: The offering of learning opportunities in professional and vocational development, personal development, and social development to adults.

classes.label: Workers education
classes.note: The education of union members to improve their bargaining skills. Do not confuse with "adult education".

classes.label: Mass education
classes.note: A large-scale undertaking aimed at disseminating information to influence the opinion of the general public. May also be used in relation to the propagation of popular culture.

classes.label: Traditional education
classes.note: That provided by societies before or alongside the introduction of a formal educational system.

classes.label: Extension education
classes.note: Instructional activities of educational institutions directed to clientele outside immediate student body.

classes.label: University extension
classes.note: Extension activity of universities organizing local short or part time courses in academic subjects to adults other than its students, usually away from the campus.

classes.label: Basic education
classes.note: A broader concept than primary schooling, comprising early child education, adult literacy programmes, and a range of nonformal activities for children, young people and adults.

classes.label: Compensatory education
classes.note: For deprived or disadvantaged students.

classes.label: Correctional education
classes.note: Educational and vocational programmes provided for adults or youth in prisons or detention centres.

classes.label: Migrant education
classes.note: Refers to the education of migrant workers and their families.

classes.label: Outdoor education
classes.note: Utilization of the outdoor environment to promote experiential learning and enrich the curriculum.

classes.label: Special needs education
classes.note: Education of students with special learning needs such as those with disabilities or learning difficulties.

vocab.term: Technical and vocational education and training

classes.label: Learning cities
classes.note: A learning city mobilizes its resources in every sector to promote inclusive learning from basic to higher education for all its residents, and fosters a culture of learning throughout life.

classes.label: Nonformal education
classes.note: Organized and systematic learning activity, often associated with work, provided outside the formal educational system.

classes.label: Community education
classes.note: Enabling process through which children and adults receive a sense of identification with their community.

classes.label: Consumer education
classes.note: Study of intelligent and effective methods of buying and using goods and services.

classes.label: Family education
classes.note: Education within and by the family.

classes.label: Home education
classes.note: Schooling provided either as an alternative to formal education or for homebound persons.

classes.label: Informal learning
classes.note: The process of learning which goes on continuously and incidentally for each individual, outside the organized situation of formal or nonformal education. Do not confuse with "nonformal education".

classes.label: Recurrent education
classes.note: Periodic professional renewal, distinct from more general concept of lifelong education.

classes.label: Out of school education
classes.note: Institutions, programmes and activities for out of school youth and extra-curricular activities for those in school.

classes.label: Universities
classes.note: Institutions of higher education with legal right to confer degrees.

classes.label: Open universities
classes.note: Higher education institutions with open admission that offer external degree programmes.

classes.label: Technological institutes
classes.note: Institutions of higher education with a strong orientation towards study and research in the technologies and sciences.

classes.label: Teacher centres
classes.note: Organized centres for teachers to meet, discuss, find resources and develop materials.

classes.label: Associated schools
classes.note: Relates to the UNESCO Associated Schools Project.

classes.label: Community schools
classes.note: Schools open beyond ordinary hours for use of students, their parents and the community.

classes.label: Disadvantaged schools
classes.note: Schools where activities, facilities or resources do not meet the basic educational needs of students.

classes.label: Nursery schools
classes.note: Institutions providing education for preschool children.

classes.label: Comprehensive schools
classes.note: Non-selective secondary schools providing all types of education.

classes.label: Special schools
classes.note: For disabled students.

classes.label: Summer schools
classes.note: Short course usually held at a university or college during the summer vacation.

classes.label: Curriculum
classes.note: Use to mean the subjects taught, the time allotted to each, and the sequence.

classes.label: Core curriculum
classes.note: Essential or basic parts of the curriculum of an educational institution that are studied by all its students even though each has a choice of optional subjects in addition.

classes.label: Extracurricular activities
classes.note: Activities organized by the school, for which participation is generally not compulsory.

classes.label: Integrated curriculum
classes.note: Systematic organization of curriculum content and parts into a meaningful pattern.

classes.label: Modular instruction
classes.note: Organization of the curriculum or of instructional courses in self-contained units ('modules') designed for management by the learner.

classes.label: Educational courses
classes.note: Administrative aspects of subject programmes. Use more specific descriptor.

classes.label: Credit courses
classes.note: Course work in higher education measured by a credit system whereby credit hours are assigned to a course defined by the number of hours per week in class and the number of weeks in the session.

classes.label: Elective courses
classes.note: Courses chosen freely by a student from among a number of alternatives.

classes.label: Postgraduate courses
classes.note: Courses of study or research at a higher education institution after completion of first degree requirements.

classes.label: Digital skills
classes.note: Comprehension of the capabilities and applications of computers. May include the ability to use computers to solve problems.

classes.label: Functional literacy
classes.note: General concept of relating literacy to improved living conditions.

classes.label: Futures literacy
classes.note: Skill that allows people to better understand the role of the future in what they see and do.

classes.label: Information literacy
classes.note: Comprises the competencies to recognize information needs and to locate, evaluate, apply and create information within cultural and social contexts

classes.label: Life skills
classes.note: The ability and readiness to face and solve demands and challenges of everyday life.

classes.label: Social and emotional learning
classes.note: Process through which children and adults understand and manage emotions, set and achieve positive goals, feel and show empathy for others, establish and maintain positive relationships, and make responsible decisions.

classes.label: Art education
classes.note: Use for drawing, graphics, painting, and sculpture.

classes.label: Speech education
classes.note: Includes various aspects of oral communication such as discussion, conversation, debate, interpretative reading and drama.

classes.label: General technical education
classes.note: Provides knowledge about production principles and processes and practical skills needed for participation in productive work.

classes.label: Population education
classes.note: Do not confuse with "family education".

classes.label: Media education
classes.note: Seeks to enable people to gain an understanding of the way the media act and operate in society, and critically analyze media messages.

classes.label: Humanities education
classes.note: Studies dealing with man as the central concern, e.g. literature, history, philosophy, and modern and classical languages.

vocab.term: Teaching and learning about the Holocaust

classes.label: Social studies
classes.note: Adaptations of knowledge from the social sciences for teaching purposes at the primary and secondary levels of education.

classes.label: Development education
classes.note: Education on the issues of concern in the development process addressed to youth and adults in developed countries.

classes.label: Inservice teacher education
classes.note: Designed to enable teachers to be retrained, or to obtain a higher level certificate, or even to be initially trained when already in the field.

classes.label: Microteaching
classes.note: An experimental teacher training method using small groups of students.

classes.label: Technical education
classes.note: Formal education designed to provide knowledge and skills underlying production processes with a wider connotation than vocational education at secondary or higher level.

classes.label: Industrial education
classes.note: All types of education related to industry including industrial arts and education for occupations in industry at all levels.

classes.label: Vocational education
classes.note: Formal education designed to prepare for skilled occupations.

classes.label: Management education
classes.note: Educational programmes to increase managerial and supervisory skills of managers and management trainees.

classes.label: Paraprofessional educational personnel
classes.note: Includes non-teaching staff whose functions are professional.

classes.label: Teachers
classes.note: Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Trainers
classes.note: Persons who direct the practice of skills toward immediate improvement in some art or task.

classes.label: Exceptional students
classes.note: Covers atypical students of any kind.

classes.label: Foreign students
classes.note: Students not native to a particular country.

classes.label: Graduates
classes.note: Individuals who have completed the requirements of a higher education and have been awarded a degree.

classes.label: Undergraduates
classes.note: Students engaged in studies leading to a first degree, e.g. bachelor's degree.

classes.label: Trainees
classes.note: Participants in vocational, administrative or technical training programmes for purpose of developing job related skills.

classes.label: Activity learning
classes.note: Learning by doing.

classes.label: Blended learning
classes.note: Learning approach that combines both remote learning and in-person learning

classes.label: Distance education
classes.note: Education imparted at a distance through the use of information/communication technology: radio, TV, the telephone, correspondence, e-mail, videoconferencing, audioconferencing, cd-roms, or online.

classes.label: Electronic learning
classes.note: Online learning via the Internet or an intranet.

classes.label: Home study
classes.note: Studying done at home outside school hours, including work on school assignments, community projects, or individual problems. Do not confuse with "Home education".

classes.label: Independent study
classes.note: Study carried out with a minimum or a complete absence of external guidance. Do not confuse with "individualized instruction".

classes.label: Practical work (learning method)
classes.note: Part of timetable where students do practical work in laboratory or workshop.

classes.label: Self instruction
classes.note: Learning by oneself without the aid of a teacher.

classes.label: Teaching
classes.note: Technical aspects of the teaching process. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Teaching methods
classes.note: Patterns of teacher behaviour that are recurrent, applicable to various subject matters, characteristic of more than one teacher and relevant to learning.

classes.label: Classroom techniques
classes.note: Techniques used in the classroom or in any other educational setting to create propitious learning conditions. Includes discipline, management, sitting arrangement.

classes.label: Competency based teaching
classes.note: Refers to specific teaching skills of interacting with students in classrooms, based on the clear definition of the knowledge, skills and attitudes to be acquired. (IBE uses: competency-based education)

classes.label: Seminars (teaching method)
classes.note: Meetings of a group of students engaged in research or advanced study under the direction of one or more leaders to discuss problems of mutual interest.

classes.label: Workshops (teaching method)
classes.note: Meetings of individuals with common interests and problems, usually with experts, to exchange information and learn needed skills or techniques.

classes.label: Tutoring
classes.note: Private intensive teaching, usually of a single student.

classes.label: Multimedia instruction
classes.note: Integration of more than one medium in a presentation or module of instruction.

classes.label: Peer teaching
classes.note: The practice of having students of the same or similar age assist with the instruction of other students who may need supplemental aid.

classes.label: Remedial instruction
classes.note: Designed to catch up with a lag in a given subject or field.

classes.label: Training
classes.note: Systematic educative process by which one learns new skills.

classes.label: Basic training
classes.note: Specially organized training, given outside of production activities of an undertaking, and aimed at imparting the basic knowledge and skill required for a given group of occupations.

classes.label: Further training
classes.note: Global term for training subsequent and complementary to initial training.

classes.label: Professional training
classes.note: Special instruction to develop skills needed to improve job performance of professional personnel, usually short term and job specific.

classes.label: Retraining
classes.note: Training for a new occupation.

classes.label: Vocational training
classes.note: Training aiming at providing the skills, knowledge and attitudes required for employment in a particular occupation, or group of related occupations, in any field of economic activity.

classes.label: Inservice training
classes.note: Training acquired during employment.

classes.label: Training courses
classes.note: Courses organized in a professional environment during or at the end of the educational process.

classes.label: Study service (higher education)
classes.note: Optional or compulsory part of a programme of studies where credit is given for work off-campus in social or development services, local government, and industrial or other organizations.

classes.label: Work experience programmes
classes.note: Instructional programmes providing for some part of the students' time to be spent in one of the sectors of production.

classes.label: Dropping out
classes.note: Premature school leaving before completing a cycle or course already begun.

classes.label: Aptitude tests
classes.note: Instruments used to assess a combination of native and acquired abilities which are considered indicative of future performance.

classes.label: Teacher evaluation
classes.note: Judging teacher performance based on established criteria.

classes.label: Teacher effectiveness
classes.note: Degree to which teachers are successful in satisfying their objectives, obligations and functions.

classes.label: Educational qualifications
classes.note: Required conditions, usually academic, for a post.

classes.label: Bachelors degrees
classes.note: First university degree.

classes.label: Diplomas
classes.note: Certificates of higher education with less weight than a degree.

classes.label: Equivalence between diplomas
classes.note: Includes all levels.

classes.label: National qualifications framework
classes.note: Instrument used to classify a country’s qualifications at different levels. Each level is defined by a set of learning outcomes expected at that level.

classes.label: Educational quality
classes.note: Degrees of excellence in meeting educational objectives. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Academic standards
classes.note: Criteria established by an educational institution to determine levels of student achievement.

classes.label: Educational accountability
classes.note: Being held responsible and answerable for specific results or outcomes of an activity (over which one has responsibility).

classes.label: Educational relevance
classes.note: Applicability of what is taught to the needs and interest of students and society.

classes.label: Teaching machines
classes.note: Devices that mechanically, electrically or electronically present instructional programmes at a rate controlled by the learner's responses.

classes.label: Teaching guides
classes.note: Manuals for teachers often accompanying textbooks.

classes.label: Lesson plans
classes.note: A teacher's outline of what he hopes to accomplish with the students during a particular lesson. It may list aims, main teaching points, media and resources, teaching and evaluation methods, etc.

classes.label: Educational technology
classes.note: Theory and application of educational media in a systematic way.

classes.label: Resource centres
classes.note: Indoor or outdoor areas that offer a variety of resources (e.g. supplies, materials, information, equipment). Use a more precise term, if possible.

classes.label: Teaching materials
classes.note: Any printed and/or nonprinted material designed specifically for or used in instruction. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Audiovisual aids
classes.note: Nonprint teaching materials and the equipment required for their display.

classes.label: Educational software
classes.note: Computer software and accompanying documentation written for educational applications.

classes.label: Learning packages
classes.note: Materials designed so that learners can learn from them without much help from a teacher: they are pre-recorded, stored teaching.

classes.label: Systems design
classes.note: Development of an integrated method for producing a required article or performing a desired operation.

classes.label: Methodology
classes.note: Study of the direction and implications of research methods and techniques, especially as to their logical basis.

classes.label: Science and society
classes.note: Relations between science as human activity and as factor of change, and social structures.

classes.label: Comparative analysis
classes.note: Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Evaluation
classes.note: Appraising or judging persons, organizations or things in relation to stated objectives, standards or criteria. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Benchmarking
classes.note: Systematic and continuous evaluation of products, services, performances or methods against a standard or agreed upon point of reference in order to achieve excellence.

classes.label: Formative evaluation
classes.note: A type of assessment essentially used to modify and improve products, programmes or activities during their planning and development.

classes.label: Quality control
classes.note: Techniques, such as inspection and regulation, that are used to ensure a uniform and/or desired quality of performance or product.

classes.label: Summative evaluation
classes.note: A type of evaluation that sums up the effects and effectiveness of a programme or activity once it is concluded.

classes.label: Simulation models
classes.note: Use only in connection with research and planning.

classes.label: Technology assessment
classes.note: Refers to the examination and evaluation of the possible consequences of the introduction of new technologies.

classes.label: Choice of technology
classes.note: Deciding on labour intensive or capital intensive methods, choosing among various manufacturing processes, etc.

classes.label: Appropriate technology
classes.note: Technology adapted to the needs, production system, and natural resources of a given country.

classes.label: Digital divide
classes.note: Disparities in access to, and use of information and communication technologies such as Internet, between as well as within countries.

classes.label: Applied research
classes.note: Research which is designed to create a new technology.

classes.label: Mission oriented research
classes.note: Research designed for the solution of a specific problem.

classes.label: Research and development
classes.note: Research directed towards the development of new products and processes.

classes.label: Fundamental research
classes.note: Research designed to produce new understanding of basic underlying principles and processes.

classes.label: Interdisciplinary research
classes.note: Research which establishes conceptual and methodological relationships among various disciplines.

classes.label: Open science
classes.note: Combines various movements and practices aiming to make scientific knowledge openly available, accessible and reusable for everyone.

classes.label: Science and development
classes.note: Refers to the integration of science and technology into the development process.

classes.label: Automation
classes.note: The act or practice of using machines that need little or no human control, especially to replace workers.

classes.label: Technicians
classes.note: Below level of professional but above clerical or labour levels.

classes.label: Technology
classes.note: The skills, knowledge, hardware, and procedures for providing useful goods and services.

classes.label: Nanotechnology
classes.note: Research and engineering conducted at the nanoscale.

classes.label: Technology transfer
classes.note: Access to new technology, both products and production techniques, as a key factor in the economic growth of developing countries.

classes.label: Diffusion of technology
classes.note: Transfer of a new technology from the first commercial user to a number of competing users.

classes.label: Know-how transfer
classes.note: Technical and managerial expertise necessary to implement a technology.

classes.label: Traditional technology
classes.note: Techniques passed from generation to generation (although some modernized components or processes may be included).

classes.label: Statistics
classes.note: Use when referring to the science of statistics. For collections of statistics, use "statistical data", or more specific descriptor, e.g. "educational statistics", etc.

classes.label: Wave mechanics
classes.note: Includes wave equations and functions.

classes.label: Solar activity
classes.note: Includes solar wind, flares, prominences, sunspots.

classes.label: Cosmology
classes.note: Nature and origin of the universe.

classes.label: Seismicity
classes.note: Frequency and distribution of earthquakes.

classes.label: Biogeography
classes.note: Geographical distribution of animals and plants.

classes.label: Human geography
classes.note: Relationship of geography and culture (population, institutions and technology).

classes.label: Palaeogeography
classes.note: Historical reconstitution of the physical geography of past ages.

classes.label: Regional geography
classes.note: Use for the study of the geographical features within an area as they interact to give the area a unique character.

classes.label: Savannah
classes.note: Treeless plains in tropical or subtropical regions.

classes.label: Steppe
classes.note: Vast treeless plains of South-eastern Europe and Siberia.

classes.label: Oceanographic research
classes.note: Use for works dealing with research projects. For general scientific works, use "oceanography".

classes.label: Climate
classes.note: Average weather of any region.

classes.label: Hydrometeorology
classes.note: The study of the occurence, movement and changes in the state of water in the atmosphere.

classes.label: Hydrological cycle
classes.note: The continuous circulation of water through evaporation and precipitation.

classes.label: Evapotranspiration
classes.note: Water loss through evaporation.

classes.label: Hydrology
classes.note: The study of the waters of the earth, their circulation, distribution and properties.

classes.label: Hydrological research
classes.note: Use for works dealing with research projects. For general scientific works, use "hydrology".

classes.label: Hydrosphere
classes.note: That part of the earth that is water e.g. oceans, lakes and rivers.

classes.label: Water balance
classes.note: The flow and storage in a hydrologic unit such as a drainage basin, a soil zone, a lake or reservoir and the relationship between evaporation, precipitation, runoff and the change in water storage.

classes.label: Water security
classes.note: Capacity of a population to safeguard access to adequate quantities of water of acceptable quality for sustaining human and ecosystem health on a watershed basis, and to ensure efficient protection of life and property against water-related hazards – floods, landslides, land subsidence and droughts.

classes.label: Energy economics
classes.note: Economics as it relates to the energy sector.

classes.label: Biological control
classes.note: Control of undesirable insects, plants or animals by the introduction of predators, parasites, or diseases.

classes.label: Environmental ethics
classes.note: Ethical reflection relating to human interaction with the natural environment

classes.label: Environmental impact assessment
classes.note: An activity designed to identify, predict, interpret and communicate information concerning the environmental consequences of policies, projects etc.

classes.label: Environmental indicators
classes.note: Numerical data used as benchmarks in the formulation and monitoring of environmental policy.

classes.label: Ecology
classes.note: Use for the study of relationships between living organisms and their natural environment.

classes.label: Ecological research
classes.note: Use for works dealing with research projects. For general scientific works, use "ecology".

classes.label: Climate change adaptation
classes.note: Initiatives and measures to reduce the vulnerability of natural and human systems against actual or expected climate change effects

classes.label: Education in emergencies
classes.note: Refers to the quality learning opportunities for all ages  in  situations  of  crisis

classes.label: Eutrophication
classes.note: Enrichment of water by nutrients, especially compounds of nitrogen and phosphorus, that will accelerate the growth of algae and higher forms of plant life, and thus deplete the oxygen level of water.

classes.label: Ecosystems
classes.note: The system of interdependent complex of plant and animal populations within a particular geographic content, generally an area of uniform environmental conditions.

classes.label: Biosphere
classes.note: That part of the earth, and the atmosphere surrounding it, which is able to support life.

classes.label: Biomass
classes.note: The mass of organisms living in an animal or plant ecosystem.

classes.label: Biomes
classes.note: The largest land community region, e.g. tundra, savannah, grassland, desert, forest. Each biome may contain several ecosystems.

classes.label: Biosphere reserves
classes.note: Reserves created to ensure long-term survival of representative ecosystems, with their component plants and animals.

classes.label: Biological adaptation
classes.note: A genetically determined characteristic that enhances the ability of an organism to cope with its environment.

classes.label: Ecosystem services
classes.note: Benefits received by society thanks to the functioning of ecosystems.

classes.label: Biomass energy
classes.note: Energy from the conversion of agricultural and forest residues, standing vegetation, energy crops, and wastes.

classes.label: Soil resources
classes.note: Use to denote the availability of soil, mainly for cultivation.

classes.label: Trace elements
classes.note: Elements combined in minute quantities in plant or animal tissues considered essential in physiological processes.

classes.label: Biosynthesis
classes.note: Production of molecules by a living cell which is essential feature of anabolism.

classes.label: Bioethics
classes.note: Study of social and ethical questions raised by development in biology and medicine.

classes.label: Biological research
classes.note: Use for works dealing with research projects. For general scientific works, use "biology".

classes.label: Biometrics
classes.note: Statistical methods applied to biological problems.

classes.label: Limnology
classes.note: Study of living organisms in freshwater.

classes.label: Radiobiology
classes.note: Biological effects of radiation.

classes.label: Space biology
classes.note: Use for the study of man or other earth life in outer space.

classes.label: Genome
classes.note: Complete genetic repertoire of an organism.

classes.label: Genes
classes.note: The fundamental physical and functional unit of heredity, responsible for specific traits.

classes.label: Genetics
classes.note: The study of inheritance patterns of specific traits.

classes.label: Biogenesis
classes.note: The theory that living organisms can arise only from other living organisms and non from nonliving matter.

classes.label: Eugenics
classes.note: Improvement of hereditary characteristics of a population or of a family by controlled or selective breeding.

classes.label: Mutation
classes.note: Any change in the genotype of an organism occurring at the gene, chromosome or genome level.

classes.label: Physiological effects
classes.note: Effects of electricity, chemicals, heat, pressure, etc. on the human body.

classes.label: Ethnobotany
classes.note: Knowledge, uses and methods of management of plant resources by communities.

classes.label: Plant taxonomy
classes.note: Classification of the species of plants.

classes.label: Vegetation
classes.note: Plant life characteristic of an ecological area. For taxonomic aspects use "flora".

classes.label: Animal taxonomy
classes.note: Classification of the species of animals.

classes.label: Epidemiology
classes.note: Study of the occurence and distribution of disease.

classes.label: Occupational medicine
classes.note: Medical care in its relation to work and the work environment.

classes.label: Occupational diseases
classes.note: Harmful effects of occupational activities and work environment on workers' health.

classes.label: Injuries
classes.note: Includes fractures, wounds, burns, etc.

classes.label: Civilization crises
classes.note: Situation in which a civilization is fundamentally called into question.

classes.label: Cultural inequality
classes.note: Disparity of levels of culture and access to it within a given society.

classes.label: Cultural minorities
classes.note: Group of persons belonging to a culture different from that of the majority of the society in which they live.

classes.label: Cultural identity
classes.note: Denotes the correspondence which exists between a community (national, ethnic, linguistic, etc.) and its cultural life, as well as the right of each community to its own culture.

classes.label: Acculturation
classes.note: Phenomena which result when groups of individuals of different cultures come into continuous contact, with subsequent changes in the original cultural patterns of either or both groups.

classes.label: Cultural isolation
classes.note: Relative lack of participation in the cultural system.

classes.label: Countercultures
classes.note: Cultural system which develops in conflict with the prevailing culture.

classes.label: Cultural diversity
classes.note: Coexistence within society of culturally differentiated groups which maintain separate ways of life.

classes.label: Culture of peace
classes.note: A culture that promotes lifeways, patterns of belief, values and behaviour that foster peace-building and accompanying institutional arrangements.

classes.label: Culture of poverty
classes.note: A set of values, beliefs, attitudes and behaviour patterns which result from persistent marginalization and exclusion, and characterize the cultural milieu of the poor.

classes.label: Scientific culture
classes.note: Pattern of intellectual and social behaviour based on scientific knowledge.

classes.label: Subcultures
classes.note: Culture peculiar to a social group or category.

classes.label: Culture
classes.note: Use more specific descriptor.

classes.label: Cultural action
classes.note: Efforts tending to develop culture in the broadest meaning of the term, with reference to community development, freedom of expression and free choice of life style.

classes.label: Cultural activities
classes.note: All types of activities tending to enhance cultural life through cultural animation and cultural values promotion. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Documentary heritage
classes.note: Valuable archive holdings and library collections of the world.

classes.label: Digital heritage
classes.note: Consists of  unique  resources  of  human  knowledge  and  expression created digitally, or converted into digital form from existing analogue resources.

classes.label: Culture and development
classes.note: Cultural dimension of the development process.

classes.label: Cultural development
classes.note: Process of development or progress in the cultural life of a community.

classes.label: Cultural indicators
classes.note: Numerical data used as benchmarks in the formulation and monitoring of cultural policy.

classes.label: Cultural relations
classes.note: Relations at both the international and intergroup level. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Cultural property preservation
classes.note: Refers to the conservation, preservation and restoration of cultural property, as well as to its protection against vandalism, theft and removal from country of origin.

classes.label: Digital preservation
classes.note: Digital preservation consists of the processes aimed at ensuring the continued accessibility of digital materials.

classes.label: Intangible cultural heritage
classes.note: A set of living practices, knowledge and representations enabling individuals and communities to express themselves through systems of values and ethical standards. Use more specific descriptor if appropriate.

classes.label: Epistemology
classes.note: The theory or science of the method or grounds of knowledge.

classes.label: Knowledge
classes.note: Information that is presented within a particular context, yielding insight on application in that context, by members of a community.

classes.label: Traditional knowledge
classes.note: Body of facts developed and maintained by a distinct cultural group as a result of direct observation and practice, including the distinctive perspective and ideas inferred from these facts.

classes.label: Metaphysics
classes.note: Includes philosophy of nature, philosophy of life, infinity, etc.

classes.label: Ontology
classes.note: The study of the essential characteristics of Being in itself apart from the study of particular existing things.

classes.label: Cults
classes.note: A particular form of religious worship, devotion to a particular person or thing.

classes.label: Archaeological sociology
classes.note: Social anthropological interpretation of archaeological remains.

classes.label: Human remains
classes.note: Use for the remains of any part of a human

classes.label: Contemporary history
classes.note: 19th-21st century.

classes.label: Modern history
classes.note: 16th-18th century.

classes.label: Chronology
classes.note: The science of computing time or periods of time and of assigning events to their true dates.

classes.label: Palaeography
classes.note: The study of ancient scripts and their development as found in manuscripts.

classes.label: Indigenous languages
classes.note: The native speech or language of a particular country or district.

classes.label: Comparative linguistics
classes.note: Study of language change and variation.

classes.label: Etymology
classes.note: Study of the origins and history of the form and meaning of words.

classes.label: Psycholinguistics
classes.note: Study of the relationships between linguistic behaviour and psychological processes, including the process of language acquisition.

classes.label: Sociolinguistics
classes.note: Social and cultural functions of language.

classes.label: Ethnolinguistics
classes.note: Study of language with reference to is cultural context.

classes.label: Acronyms
classes.note: A pronounceable abbreviation of a compound, name or phrase used as one word.

classes.label: Transcription
classes.note: System of writing the sounds of a word in one language using the script of another language.

classes.label: Transliteration
classes.note: Representation of a lexical item recorded in one writing system by means of the signs and symbols of another.

classes.label: Bosnian
classes.note: Use for works on the language of the Bosnians treated as a separate language. For works on the language(s) of Serbs, Croats and Bosnians treated together as a single language, use Serbocroatian.

classes.label: Croatian
classes.note: Use for works on the language of the Croats treated as a separate language. For works on the language(s) of the Serbs, Croats and Bosnians treated together as a single language, use Serbocroatian.

classes.label: Serbian
classes.note: Use for works on the language of the Serbs treated as a separate language. For works on the language(s) of the Serbs, Croats and Bosnians treated together as a single language, use Serbocroatian.

classes.label: Serbocroatian
classes.note: Use for works on the language(s) of the Serbs, Croats and Bosnians treated together as a single language.

classes.label: Contemporary literature
classes.note: Literature of the 20th century.

classes.label: Art styles
classes.note: Use for individual art styles, such as Renaissance, Gothic, Baroque, Impressionism, etc.

classes.label: Contemporary art
classes.note: Art of the 20th-21st century.

classes.label: Digital art
classes.note: Art created using digital technologies.

classes.label: Modern art
classes.note: 17-19th century.

classes.label: Art theory
classes.note: Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Iconography
classes.note: The branch of art history dealing with the identification, description, classification and interpretation of the subject-matter of the figurative arts.

classes.label: Musical forms
classes.note: Includes concertos, sonatas, symphonies, etc.

classes.label: Traditional music
classes.note: Music distinctive of a certain region or ethnic group.

classes.label: Ecotourism
classes.note: Environmentally friendly and socially responsible tourism.

classes.label: Behavioural sciences
classes.note: Any science that studies human and animal behaviour in its physical and social environment by experimental and observational methods.

classes.label: Participatory research
classes.note: Research approach that calls for interaction between the researchers and those among whom the research is conducted.

classes.label: Cognition
classes.note: The mental action or process of acquiring knowledge through thought, experience and senses.

classes.label: Developmental psychology
classes.note: Study of the changes in cognitive, motivational, psychophysiological, and social functioning that occur throughout the human life span.

classes.label: Aptitude
classes.note: The potential ability of an individual to perform an as yet unlearned task or skill.

classes.label: Psychological schools
classes.note: Freudian, Jungian, Gestalt, dynamic, introspective, etc.

classes.label: Group dynamics
classes.note: The way in which members of a group react to each other.

classes.label: Socialization
classes.note: Process through which individuals internalize the values, beliefs and norms of a society and learn to function as its members.

classes.label: Social capital
classes.note: A combination of social norms (such as trusts), social networks, relations and ties held by an individual or predominant within a group.

classes.label: Modernization
classes.note: Process of change in a society or social institution in which the most recent ways, ideas or styles are adapted or acquired.

classes.label: Working class
classes.note: A social class comprising those who do manual labour for wage, especially those who do not own any property. Use only when indexing historical works.

classes.label: Social status
classes.note: Position in a community relative to other members of the community.

classes.label: Elderly
classes.note: Beyond the customary age of retirement.

classes.label: Malnutrition
classes.note: Includes calorie, protein and/or vitamin deficiencies.

classes.label: Gender-based violence
classes.note: Violence directed against a person because of that person’s gender, gender identity or gender expression, or which affects persons of a particular gender disproportionately.

classes.label: Counselling
classes.note: Giving advice, information or encouragement to people in need.

classes.label: Coloureds
classes.note: Use only with respect to the ethnic group so designated in South Africa.

classes.label: Youth
classes.note: Use more specific descriptor.

classes.label: Demography
classes.note: Use for theoretical works dealing with human populations, concerned with their size, structure, distribution, growth and migration.

classes.label: Population distribution
classes.note: Physical arrangement and location of populations.

classes.label: Population research
classes.note: Use for works dealing with research projects. For general works, use "demography".

classes.label: Homemakers
classes.note: Also narrower than: Households.

classes.label: Displaced persons
classes.note: Persons who have fled or been driven from their communities to localities within their home country. For persons forced to leave their home country, use "refugees".

classes.label: Exiles
classes.note: Individuals expelled from their home country by official authority for political reasons.

classes.label: Brain drain
classes.note: The loss suffered by a country as a result of the emigration of trained professionals and technicians.

classes.label: Internal migration
classes.note: Within a country.

classes.label: Rural migration
classes.note: The migration of rural workers to urban areas.

classes.label: Population
classes.note: Use only with respect to population of a specific country or region. Otherwise, use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Population dynamics
classes.note: Population activity in terms of decline, increase or stabilization.

classes.label: Ageing population
classes.note: Continuing increase of elderly population both in absolute and in proportional terms in a given society.

classes.label: Population programmes
classes.note: Activities of international organizations in the population field.

classes.label: Sex
classes.note: The biological characteristics which define humans as female or male.

classes.label: Community centres
classes.note: Local centres for all kinds of academic and recreational activities.

classes.label: Self help
classes.note: At the community level.

classes.label: Human settlements
classes.note: Consist of shelter, infrastructure, services required by a community for the fulfillment of its functions as a social body.

classes.label: Cultural landscapes
classes.note: Illustrative of the evolution of human society and settlement over time, under the influence of the physical constraints/opportunities of the natural environment and of successive social, economic and cultural forces.

classes.label: Sacred sites
classes.note: Natural landscapes such as stones, cliffs, mountains, trees, forests, sources, lakes or rivers being regarded as of a marked religious or spiritual significance.

classes.label: Urban spaces
classes.note: Includes market places, town squares, urban parks, playgrounds, etc.

classes.label: Regional economy
classes.note: Use when referring to regions within a country.

classes.label: Regional planning
classes.note: Refers to regions within a country.

classes.label: Rural extension
classes.note: Includes training for farmers in more efficient practices, planning and management skills, low-interest credit, simple irrigation, subsidized fertilizer and post-harvest facilities, etc.

classes.label: Industrial areas
classes.note: Areas, usually urban, with a relatively high industrial concentration, either planned or unplanned.

classes.label: Urbanization
classes.note: Population concentration in urban areas as a result of rural migration or due to an increase in the number of urban areas. Do not confuse with "urban development".

classes.label: Cybernetics
classes.note: The science of control and communication, specifically the interaction between automatic control and people.

classes.label: Indexing languages
classes.note: An artificial language used by documentation systems for purposes of indexing.

classes.label: Subject headings
classes.note: A word, term or a phrase chosen to express a concept or a concept combination in indexing and to constitute an entry.

classes.label: Terminological control
classes.note: Controls that synonyms and near-synonyms are cross-referenced equivalently and homonyms and polysemes are distinguished by qualifiers.

classes.label: Thesauri
classes.note: A controlled and dynamic documentary language containing semantically and generically related terms, which comprehensively covers a specific domain of knowledge.

classes.label: Information
classes.note: Data that has been organized in such a way that it achieves meaning, in a generalized way.

classes.label: Film strips
classes.note: A strip of motion picture carrying a still photograph, or other graphic material, on each of its frames. Widely used as an audiovisual instruction tool.

classes.label: Documentation
classes.note: The continuous and systematic processing of documents or data for specialized information users.

classes.label: Bibliology
classes.note: The systematic study of the properties and characteristics of books in relation to the publication process or to the techniques of printing, production and marketing.

classes.label: ISBD
classes.note: International standard bibliographic description.

classes.label: ISBN
classes.note: International standard book number.

classes.label: ISSN
classes.note: International standard serial number.

classes.label: Communication
classes.note: An interactive social process which involves the sharing of information, experiences, and cultures, both physically or electronically, and results in the mutual enhancement of all concerned. Use more specific descriptor.

classes.label: Internet governance
classes.note: The development and application by Governments, the private sector and civil society, in their respective roles, of shared principles, norms, rules, decision-making procedures, and programmes that shape the evolution and use of the Internet.

classes.label: Communication and development
classes.note: The use of the various forms of physical communications infrastructure and the media in the development process.

classes.label: Open access
classes.note: Knowledge resources made available for public access or public consumption at large scale, without any hindrance of subscription fee or access charges.

classes.label: Open data
classes.note: Practice of publishing (raw) data in a way that is accessible, reusable, machine readable and licensed permissively. Can be generated by a wide range of parties, including public authorities, the semi-public sector, businesses and the public.

classes.label: Media diversity
classes.note: Refers to the availability of sufficient variety of media content.

classes.label: Media pluralism
classes.note: Refers to a sufficient variety of media outlets provided by a range of private, public and non-profit owners.

classes.label: Conferences
classes.note: Use only when referring to their organization, financing, etc.

classes.label: Intercultural dialogue
classes.note: Verbal and nonverbal communication among people of different cultures.

classes.label: Public information
classes.note: Information, offered by governmental and corporate bodies to the public, to disseminate knowledge concerning the programmes and activities of the institution.

classes.label: Information theory
classes.note: Includes the coding and decoding of messages.

classes.label: Information and development
classes.note: Refers to the contribution of scientific and social science information to the development process.

classes.label: Programme content
classes.note: In the field of communication.

classes.label: Editors
classes.note: A person who is responsible for, or prepares for publication, the contents of a document to which he may or may not have contributed.

classes.label: Information scientists
classes.note: A person who works on the theory or application of informatics or information science, i.e. analyses, designs, implements etc. information systems.

classes.label: Press
classes.note: Newspapers, journals, periodicals, and their publishing.

classes.label: Publishing
classes.note: Making a record of knowledge available to the public as a publication.

classes.label: Public archives
classes.note: (1) In general usage, records accumulated by government agencies. (2) Records open to public inspection by law or custom.

classes.label: Data centres
classes.note: An organization handling and providing mainly numerical data usually without evaluation.

classes.label: Document delivery
classes.note: Providing users of information with the documents that they request.

classes.label: Geographical information systems
classes.note: An information system containing geographically referenced information for use in decision-making in several domains, most of which relate to the human use of the physical environment.

classes.label: Digital libraries
classes.note: Organized collections of information resources in digital or electronic format along with the services designed to help users identify and use those collections.

classes.label: National libraries
classes.note: A 'library' which is responsible for acquiring and conserving copies of all significant publications published in the country and may function as a "legal deposit library".

classes.label: Depository libraries
classes.note: A 'library' receiving by law or under arrangements free copies of all or all required national publications.

classes.label: Public libraries
classes.note: A library which serves the population of a community or region free of charge or for a nominal fee.

classes.label: Special libraries
classes.note: A library primarily serving one discipline or particular field.

classes.label: Conference papers
classes.note: Use only when referring to their writing, editing, etc.

classes.label: Glossaries
classes.note: A vocabulary not necessarily in alphabetic order, with definitions or explanations for all terms.

classes.label: Machine readable materials
classes.note: Information coded by methods requiring the use of a computer for processing.

classes.label: Monographs
classes.note: (1) A treatise on a single subject. (2) In cataloguing, any publication which is not "serials".

classes.label: Primary documents
classes.note: An original "document" which is not the result of a documentation process.

classes.label: Yearbooks
classes.note: An annual 'volume' of current information in descriptive and/or statistical form, sometimes limited to a special field.

classes.label: Secondary documents
classes.note: A document containing data or information about "primary documents".

classes.label: Accessions lists
classes.note: A list of new acquisitions issued periodically.

classes.label: Anthologies
classes.note: A collection of works of various authors or of one author selected for a specific purpose or under specific aspects.

classes.label: Abstracts
classes.note: The usually non-critical indication of the subject contents of a document, aiming to permit the user a decision about the relevance of the document.

classes.label: Bibliographies
classes.note: A printed list of documents containing formal descriptions of the documents.

classes.label: National bibliographies
classes.note: A bibliography of books produced in one country whatever their language and/or in the language of one country.

classes.label: Catalogues
classes.note: An ordered compilation of bibliographic descriptions and sufficient information to afford access to the documents.

classes.label: Directories
classes.note: A list of persons or organizations systematically or alphabetically arranged giving some information about the single units, usually at least the addresses.

classes.label: Indexes
classes.note: An ordered reference list of the contents of a file or document together with references for identification or location of those contents.

classes.label: Literature reviews
classes.note: A survey of progress in a particular field of science over a given period.

classes.label: Quotations
classes.note: A note of reference to a work from which a passage is quoted or to some source material as authority for a statement or proposition.

classes.label: Serials
classes.note: A publication issued in separate and successive parts usually in a uniform format with constant title and intended to be continued indefinitely.

classes.label: UNESCO coupons
classes.note: Used for purchasing publications and audiovisual materials intended for educational, scientific, and cultural purposes.

classes.label: Information dissemination
classes.note: The supply of information or records from a storage point to persons or organizations.

classes.label: International circulation of materials
classes.note: Use only in relation to agreements that aim to facilitate the international exchange of materials intended for educational, scientific and cultural purposes.

classes.label: Selective dissemination of information
classes.note: A service which continually disseminates documents, references, "abstracts" or data selected according to the interest profiles of the users.

classes.label: Information processing
classes.note: The storage and processing of items of information.

classes.label: Indexing
classes.note: Assignment of index terms to documents or objects with the aim to be able later on to retrieve the documents or objects according to the selected concepts designated by the index terms (essentially, descriptors).

classes.label: Search strategies
classes.note: An analysis and formulation of the optimum methods by which a particular search question may be answered by a retrieval system.

classes.label: Library circulation
classes.note: Lending to users the documents requested.

classes.label: Records management
classes.note: That area of general administrative management concerned with achieving economy and efficiency in the creation, use and maintenance, and disposition of records.

classes.label: Computer applications
classes.note: Use more specific term if appropriate.

classes.label: Artificial intelligence
classes.note: Capability of a device to perform functions normally associated with human intelligence.

classes.label: Expert systems
classes.note: Computer system based on a data base created by human authorities on a particular subject.

classes.label: Robotics
classes.note: An area of artificial intelligence applied to the industrial use of robots for performance of repetitive tasks.

classes.label: Data processing
classes.note: Systematic handling, manipulation, and computation of data, always involving the use of computers. Do not confuse with "information processing".

classes.label: Digitization
classes.note: Conversion of paper image or any other traditional document support into electronic image.

classes.label: Encoding
classes.note: "Data transformation" or representation applying a "code".

classes.label: Remote sensing
classes.note: An advanced system of information gathering to monitor and forecast developments on the surface of the earth and identify an area's natural resources by looking at the world from aircraft, balloons, or satellites and evaluating the data gathered.

classes.label: Information technology
classes.note: Includes technology for data base management systems, as well as for information distribution, such as teleprocessing systems, networks of terminals, videotex systems, micrography, etc.

classes.label: Telematics
classes.note: Data transfer services via telecommunication systems.

classes.label: Electronic mail
classes.note: Includes message creation, electronic mail and electronic filing.

classes.label: Teleconferencing
classes.note: Conducting conferences simultaneously at dispersed locations using video, telephone or related media.

classes.label: Internet universality
classes.note: Advocates for an Internet that is based on human Rights, that is Open and Accessible to all, and nurtured by Multistakeholder participation (ROAM principles).

classes.label: Microprocessors
classes.note: The computer's central processing unit.

classes.label: Neighbouring rights
classes.note: Rights of performers, producers of phonograms and broadcasting organizations.

classes.label: Piracy
classes.note: Unauthorized reproduction, importing or distribution of works protected by copyright or neighbouring rights.

classes.label: Public domain
classes.note: Publicly accessible information, the use of which does not infringe any legal right, or any obligation of confidentiality.

classes.label: Legal status
classes.note: The standing of an individual or a group before the law which determines rights and duties.

classes.label: Landlocked countries
classes.note: Use with respect to legal issues such as access to the sea and right to participate in the exploitation of marine resources.

classes.label: Law
classes.note: Use for works concerning the science of law. For individual laws, use "legislation", "environmental legislation", etc.

classes.label: Consensus
classes.note: An opinion that all or the majority of a group agree with.

classes.label: Rights of special groups
classes.note: Do not use as a descriptor.

classes.label: Gender equality
classes.note: Equal rights, responsibilities and opportunities of women and men and girls and boys.

classes.label: Governance
classes.note: Manner in which power and authority are exercised by both public and private bodies. Includes such issues as public sector management, legal framework, accountability and transparency.

classes.label: Electronic governance
classes.note: The public sector's use of information and communication technologies with the aim of improving information and service delivery, encouraging citizen participation in the decision-making process and making government more accountable, transparent and effective.

classes.label: Women in politics
classes.note: Women as office-holders, political party functionaries, etc. For political participation of women in general, use "womens participation" and "politics", or "womens suffrage".

classes.label: Regionalism
classes.note: Use only in a subnational context.

classes.label: Civic engagement
classes.note: Any individual or group activity addressing issues of public concern.

classes.label: International cooperation
classes.note: All forms of cooperation on an international basis.

classes.label: Foreign aid
classes.note: Aid from the viewpoint of the donor country.

classes.label: Global public goods
classes.note: A public good with benefits that are strongly universal in terms of countries, people and both current and future generations.

classes.label: Global commons
classes.note: Resources or zones that are shared as common property by all nations.

classes.label: Humanitarian assistance
classes.note: Any material assistance or intercession by the international community in troubled areas for purely humanitarian ends.

classes.label: Regional cooperation
classes.note: Cooperation for development in any economic, social or technical field at the supranational level.

classes.label: Regional organizations
classes.note: Groupings of countries for economic, political, or military purposes.

classes.label: South South relations
classes.note: Relations among developing countries.

classes.label: Peace agreements
classes.note: Agreements, not necessarily in written form, between parties within a country.

classes.label: Peacebuilding
classes.note: Action to identify and support structures which will tend to strengthen peace in order to avoid a relapse into conflict.

classes.label: Peacekeeping
classes.note: Action linked with the deployment of UN military and/or police personnel in areas of instability, with the consent of all the parties concerned.

classes.label: Peacemaking
classes.note: Action to bring hostile parties to agreement through means foreseen in chapter VI of the UN Charter concerning the peaceful settlement of disputes.

classes.label: Business cycles
classes.note: Alternate expansion and contraction in overall economic activity.

classes.label: Capital intensity
classes.note: Relatively greater plant and equipment costs than labour costs.

classes.label: Labour intensity
classes.note: Relatively greater labour costs than plant and equipment costs.

classes.label: Economic growth
classes.note: Refers to the increased output of goods and services. Do not confuse with "economic and social development".

classes.label: Green economy
classes.note: Economy which is low-carbon, resource efficient, and socially inclusive.

classes.label: Economic structure
classes.note: Relative importance of the various sectors of the economy.

classes.label: Economic cooperation
classes.note: Includes cooperative measures in banking, trade, industry etc., between and among countries.

classes.label: Economic integration
classes.note: At the international level.

classes.label: Common markets
classes.note: Agreement between two or more countries to abolish restrictions on the movement of capital and labour as well as trade restrictions among themselves.

classes.label: Structural adjustment
classes.note: Government austerity measures directed towards altering the structure of the economy.

classes.label: Dual economy
classes.note: Economy in which a modern, capital-intensive sector coexists with an impoverished, traditional sector.

classes.label: Mixed economy
classes.note: Economy in which elements of government control are intermingled with market elements in organizing production and consumption.

classes.label: Informal sector
classes.note: Refers to the unofficial, or non-registered and untaxed, therefore informal, sector of the economy.

classes.label: Comparative advantage
classes.note: A country's ability to provide certain products and services relatively more cheaply than other products or services.

classes.label: Economic equilibrium
classes.note: A state of balance between the various economic forces.

classes.label: International division of labour
classes.note: Theory and practice of international planning and agreements by which countries specialize in the production of those commodities for which they have the greatest comparative advantage. Do not confuse with "division of labour".

classes.label: Macroeconomics
classes.note: An economic study devoted to examining the function of a country's or region's economy or the international economy as a whole.

classes.label: Microeconomics
classes.note: That part of the study of economics devoted to the behaviour of people, governments and organizations in specific markets.

classes.label: Income and wealth
classes.note: Use more specific descriptor.

classes.label: Income
classes.note: Income of an individual or an organization. Otherwise use "national income".

classes.label: Remittances
classes.note: Transfer of funds by emigrants or migrant workers to their country or region of origin.

classes.label: Interdependence
classes.note: Mutual economic dependence among countries. For active efforts to promote closer economic ties, use "economic cooperation", "economic integration", etc.

classes.label: Economic relations
classes.note: Refers only to bilateral relations between countries.

classes.label: Dependence
classes.note: Situation in which a country's economy is subordinated to the development of another country's economy.

classes.label: Globalization
classes.note: Market-driven transnationalization of economic relations (trade, foreign investment, financial flows), which leads to a deepening of economic interdependence and consequently, erodes the capacity of governments to regulate the national economy.

classes.label: Gross national product
classes.note: The output of goods and services in a given country.

classes.label: Tied aid
classes.note: The practice of requiring that funds provided to a developing country be used to procure goods and services in the donor country.

classes.label: Private aid
classes.note: Aid provided by churches, foundations, etc.

classes.label: Technical cooperation
classes.note: Transfer of skills and provision of advice to developing countries in various fields: administrative, scientific, professional, and technical.

classes.label: Economic and social development
classes.note: Use more specific descriptor when appropriate.

classes.label: Development policy
classes.note: A definite course or method of action selected from among development alternatives. Use more specific descriptors where appropriate.

classes.label: Development indicators
classes.note: Numerical data used as benchmarks in the formulation and monitoring of development policy.

classes.label: Feasibility studies
classes.note: They identify and prepare a preliminary design of the technical and institutional alternatives that may exist for a proposed project.

classes.label: Development strategies
classes.note: The coordinated package of programmes and projects dictated by development policy, which aims to achieve a particular kind of development.

classes.label: Basic needs
classes.note: The minimum requirements for a decent standard of life: adequate food, shelter, clothing, community services. They also include needs relating to human rights, public participation in decision-making, productive employment.

classes.label: Capacity building
classes.note: Implies the enhancement of capabilities of people and institutions to improve their competence and problem solving capacities in a sustainable manner.

classes.label: Endogenous development
classes.note: Based on the socio-cultural characteristics of a country, rather than on its integration into the world economy.

classes.label: Human development
classes.note: A process of enlarging people's choices: focuses on both the formation of human capabilities - improved health, knowledge and skills - and the use people make of their acquired capabilities, for work or leisure.

classes.label: Empowerment
classes.note: Enabling individuals or communities to take charge and make full use of their knowledge, energies and judgment.

classes.label: Human security
classes.note: Protecting the vital core of all human lives in ways that enhance human freedoms and human fulfilment

classes.label: Integrated development
classes.note: Development taking into account a range of factors characteristic of the human condition.

classes.label: Participatory development
classes.note: Institutionalization of popular participation in the development process.

classes.label: Civil society
classes.note: Organized and legally bound social life that is voluntary and autonomous from the State, such as nongovernmental organizations, associations and grassroot movements.

classes.label: Self reliance
classes.note: Reliance primarily on a country's own human and natural resources and the capacity for autonomous goal-setting and decision-making.

classes.label: Sustainable development
classes.note: Environmentally sound development, which meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

classes.label: Women and development
classes.note: Integration of women into the development process.

classes.label: Reconstruction
classes.note: Recovery and rehabilitation activities following war or large scale devastation.

classes.label: Economic reintegration
classes.note: Use for ex-combatants and returning civilians.

classes.label: Development theory
classes.note: A highly interdisciplinary field involving all the social sciences, in addition to economics, also sociology and anthropology, demography, geography, health research, education, agricultural and other natural sciences, etc.

classes.label: Food security
