classes.note: Access by all people at all times to enough food for an active, healthy life.

classes.label: Agrarian structure
classes.note: A complex of relationships which exist among land tenure, production and supporting services, and related rural institutions, each constituting an integral part of the wider whole.

classes.label: Agricultural research
classes.note: Designed to improve crops, increase yields, develop resistances to diseases.

classes.label: Agronomy
classes.note: The science of crop and soil management.

classes.label: Dry farming
classes.note: A system of producing crops in arid and semi-arid regions without the use of irrigation.

classes.label: Shifting cultivation
classes.note: Temporary use of agricultural land for cultivation as long as it is fertile.

classes.label: Agroforestry
classes.note: Simultaneous growing of trees with food crops and/or livestock on the same piece of land.

classes.label: Forest management
classes.note: Refers to timber extraction and reforestation aspects of forestry.

classes.label: Silviculture
classes.note: A sector of forestry that deals with the development, reproduction and care of forest trees.

classes.label: Industrialization
classes.note: Refers to the initial stage of industrial development.

classes.label: Agroindustry
classes.note: The integration of agricultural production, processing and marketing under a single comprehensive management.

classes.label: Building operations
classes.note: Includes brick-laying, joinery, plastering, glazing, decorating, etc.

classes.label: Civil engineering
classes.note: Use for construction work other than buildings.

classes.label: Biotechnology
classes.note: Utilization of biological organisms, processes and systems to make or modify products, to improve plants or animals, or to develop microorganisms for specific uses.

classes.label: Green chemistry
classes.note: Design of products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use and generation of hazardous substances.

classes.label: Pharmaceutical technology
classes.note: Includes drugs, toiletries and cosmetics technology.

classes.label: Ergonomics
classes.note: The optimal adaptation of the work environment to human needs.

classes.label: Geoengineering
classes.note: Refers to a broad set of methods and technologies that aim to deliberately alter the climate system in order to alleviate the impacts of climate change.

classes.label: Automatic control
classes.note: Production in which all controls are automatically carried out by machinery.

classes.label: Metalworking
classes.note: Includes forging, forming, sheet metalworking, drawing, extrusion, rolling, tube-making, etc.

classes.label: Petroleum products
classes.note: Includes light oils, gas oils, fuel oils, greases, etc.

classes.label: Commodities
classes.note: As opposed to semi-manufactured or finished products, materials in their original state, or processed only enough to be prepared for marketing in international trade.

classes.label: Space stations
classes.note: Includes orbiting space stations, lunar bases, etc.

classes.label: Transport
classes.note: Refers to both transportation and transport of goods. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Debts
classes.note: Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

classes.label: Budget contributions
classes.note: Includes both voluntary and assessed contributions.

classes.label: Microcredit
classes.note: Appropriate small-scale financial support for poverty alleviation.

classes.label: Public debt
classes.note: Refers to both internal and external indebtedness.

classes.label: Debt relief
classes.note: Use with respect to a country's external public debt.

classes.label: Terms of trade
classes.note: The ratio of export to import prices of the products involved in a given country or region's international trade. May also be used by extension with respect to trade between areas within a country, such as urban or rural areas.

classes.label: Joint ventures
classes.note: Project involving enterprises or organizations that combine theory, know-how, capital and/or labour to reach a common objective.

classes.label: Transnational corporations
classes.note: Companies operating in a number of countries but with service and even production facilities frequently located outside those countries.

classes.label: Management
classes.note: Use in connection with three main tasks: supervision of and responsibility for the work of others, allocating labour, material and capital to produce a high return, and decision making.

classes.label: Knowledge management
classes.note: Development of new knowledge or absorption of existing knowledge, its organization and diffusion with the overall aim of optimizing results.

classes.label: Decentralization
classes.note: Dispersion or distribution of functions and powers from a central authority to a local authority or community.

classes.label: Management audit
classes.note: The systematic appraisal of management methods by teams from either the organization or outside.

classes.label: Quality circles
classes.note: A group of workers, performing similar work and trained to identify and solve problems, who volunteer to make recommendations relating to the improvement of productivity, quality, work morale, etc.

classes.label: Management by objectives
classes.note: Setting targets within an organization in order to achieve greater efficiency.

classes.label: Operations research
classes.note: Application of scientific methods to the analysis of problems so as to provide optimum solutions for decision making.

classes.label: Work study
classes.note: Detailed examination of the manner in which a particular job is performed, with a view to rationalizing performance and increasing productivity.

classes.label: Youth organizations
classes.note: Organizations outside school.

classes.label: Stakeholders
classes.note: An individual, group, institution, or government with an interest or concern in a particular measure taken or a proposal made by an organization.

classes.label: Career development
classes.note: The continuous planning carried out to advance a person's career based on experience and on any training undertaken to upgrade qualifications or to acquire new ones.

classes.label: Occupational status
classes.note: Employment rank, position or status achieved by an individual or group.

classes.label: Professional personnel
classes.note: For more specific descriptors, see "occupations" and "personnel".

classes.label: Personnel management
classes.note: Refers to all management decisions affecting the nature of the relationship between the organization and its employees, i.e. its human resources.

classes.label: Conditions of employment
classes.note: Use for the conditions of employment stipulated in the staff regulations of an enterprise or organization, or in a collective agreement negotiated by employer's and workers' representatives.

classes.label: Working conditions
classes.note: The physical, social and managerial factors affecting a worker's job environment.

classes.label: Labour standards
classes.note: Standards concerning employment and working conditions set out in collective agreements between employers and workers or in labour laws and regulations adopted by the legislature.

classes.label: Occupational sociology
classes.note: Sociology applied to the world of work, e.g. the workplace as a social system, occupational status, intergroup relations in the enterprise, etc.

classes.label: Occupational psychology
classes.note: The application of psychology to the work environment and personnel management.

classes.label: Recruitment
classes.note: Policies and procedures for seeking qualified employees.

classes.label: Job description
classes.note: Recognized list of functions and tasks included in a particular job.

classes.label: Job evaluation
classes.note: Determination by objective procedures of the relative value of individual jobs in an organization for such purposes as wage determination and promotion.

classes.label: Occupational qualifications
classes.note: The combined aptitudes and skills which permit someone to take up a job.

classes.label: Wages
classes.note: Payment made for work performed.

classes.label: Clandestine employment
classes.note: Gainful occupation carried out in violation of provisions set by legislation.

classes.label: Employment creation
classes.note: The generation of new jobs in sectors or enterprises requiring more manpower.

classes.label: Employment services
classes.note: Services provided officially by governments as well as those run on a private fee-paying basis.

classes.label: Full employment
classes.note: Situation where all persons seeking employment have been provided with paid positions.

classes.label: Part time employment
classes.note: Employment on a regular basis for hours substantially shorter than the standard hours.

classes.label: Structural unemployment
classes.note: Caused by changes in the structure of the economy resulting from such factors as technological change or relocation of industry, or by changes in the composition of the labour force.

classes.label: Underemployment
classes.note: Underutilization or inefficient use of the labour force.

classes.label: Division of labour
classes.note: The process whereby labour is allocated to the activity in which it is most productive.

classes.label: Human resources
classes.note: The actual workforce (manpower), plus the potential workforce.

classes.label: Labour mobility
classes.note: Ability of individual workers to move in and among labour markets.

classes.label: Manpower planning
classes.note: Analysis and projection of current manpower needs as well as future needs in light of long-term economic planning.

classes.label: Labour productivity
classes.note: Efficiency of production at the level of the individual, the enterprise or the specific economic sector.

classes.label: Labour supply
classes.note: Denotes not only the size of the workforce, but also its skills and geographic location as well as its willingness and ability to be productive.

classes.label: Manpower needs
classes.note: General demand for labour, or demand in particular industries or sectors of the economy.

classes.label: Manpower
classes.note: The economically active population.

classes.label: Labour relations
classes.note: Collective relations between employers and employees, between employers and trade unions, or between employers, unions and the government. Use "personnel management" for individual relations between employers and employees.

classes.label: Collective bargaining
classes.note: The process by which representatives of employers and employees discuss and negotiate the various phases of their relationship with a view to arriving at a mutually acceptable labour agreement.

classes.label: Collective agreements
classes.note: Agreement concerning the working conditions of a particular group of workers concluded between the workers' representatives and the employers.
